claims.text: Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally produced single-phase ZrB2 typically has inherent porosity.
Mechanically pre-activating ZrB2 powder and then using SPS can achieve full densification below 2300 °C.
SPS produces lower porosity and fewer defects than conventional sintering of ZrB2.
Reduced porosity and defect density improve resistance to degradation caused by a liquid plating bath.
Rapid pulsed current and applied pressure during SPS permit densification of ZrB2 below 2300 °C.
The rapid heating and shorter hold times of SPS enhance densification and refine the ZrB2 microstructure.
Rapid heating and shorter SPS hold times greatly reduce residual porosity.
Pulsed current and applied pressure enhance mass transport and local heating during SPS.
Enhanced mass transport and local heating enable ZrB2 sintering at a lower overall temperature.
Rapid SPS densification minimizes grain growth and porosity formation.
A more homogeneous and robust ZrB2 microstructure is less susceptible to hole formation during long-term exposure to corrosive plating baths.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have higher density than conventionally high-temperature-sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength and fewer microstructural defects than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Higher density, greater strength, and fewer defects will enhance resistance to damage during prolonged liquid-plating exposure.
The higher porosity and structural defects of conventionally sintered ZrB2 facilitate liquid-induced degradation.
